Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement has a few quick questions we need clarified before we can issue a PO:

1) Invoice cadence & net terms — the legal team prefers Net 60 for our vendor payments. Is Net 60 acceptable, or can you confirm Net 30/45 options and any tradeoffs?
2) Billing entity & VAT — which Redwood legal entity will invoice us for EU services? Will Redwood invoice gross (including VAT) or do you support reverse-charge?
3) Activation fee & prepay — your order form lists a one-time activation fee. Is that invoiced upfront or net of activation?
4) Minimum commit proration — can you confirm how minimum commit is calculated if we ramp mid-quarter?
5) Attachments — attached our standard PO template (UmbrellaSoft_PO_template.pdf).

We’re trying to get this over the finish line this week. Please loop in your legal/finance contacts (if different from sales) and provide a short answer to each point.

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — great questions. Short answers below, then I’ll flag a couple items for legal/ops: 

1) Net terms: Our standard is Net 45 for new commercial agreements. We can accept Net 60 for enterprise deals with a small commercial concession (we typically require either a quarterly prepay or a small increase to the activation fee to offset credit risk). If you need Net 60 as the default, we can propose Net 60 with first-quarter prepay or a 2% fee on outstanding balance.

2) Billing entity & VAT: For EU customers we will invoice from Redwood EU Ltd (Ireland). We normally invoice gross; however, we can support reverse-charge where applicable — we require your VAT number and a short VAT self-certification (or evidence of reverse-charge eligibility) before issuing net invoices.

3) Activation fee: The activation fee is invoiced as a separate one-time invoice on contract execution (due per the net terms you agree). If you prefer it to be paid upfront by PO, we can mark it as 'due on receipt' and include it on the first invoice.

4) Minimum commit proration: Commits are pro-rated by calendar month. If you start mid-month we invoice the prorated monthly minimum for that first partial month; minimums then follow the schedule in the pricing appendix (monthly snapshots). If you ramp or step down mid-quarter we reconcile at quarter-end (credits/refunds only for overpayment versus usage). Karthik — see legal caveat below.

5) PO: happy to accept your PO template. Please include the PO number and billing contact on signature.

I attached a quick redline doc with our suggested drafting for net terms and the tax appendix so procurement/legal can review.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben (account exec) and Karthik from legal for any redline questions.

Best,

Subject: Re: Order Form: commercial terms & procurement QA

Hi Sarah —

Following Naomi’s note, a few legal/ops clarifications to make sure procurement has what it needs: 

• Net 60 option: We can accept Net 60 on this order form under two mutually acceptable conditions: (a) UmbrellaSoft provides a valid PO covering the first 90 days of spend, or (b) UmbrellaSoft agrees to a first-quarter prepay (applied to invoices) with Net 60 thereafter. If neither is acceptable we will keep standard Net 45.

• VAT / reverse charge: To support reverse charge, please provide UmbrellaSoft’s EU VAT registration number and a signed VAT self-declaration (we can provide a template). If reverse charge is not applicable, Redwood EU Ltd will invoice VAT gross at the local rate. Also note that for some non-EU jurisdictions we may need additional tax forms.

• Activation fee / invoicing cadence: Activation fee billed on execution as a standalone invoice. Regular usage invoices are monthly in arrears unless you request consolidated quarterly billing (we charge a small administrative fee for quarterly consolidation).

• Minimum commit & proration: Our commercial team defines minimum commits in the pricing appendix per quarter. For mid-quarter starts, proration is by calendar month; quarterly reconciliations are allowed but credits only apply against future invoices, not as cash refunds. If UmbrellaSoft needs a different reconciliation model we can document a carve-out in the appendix but it requires Finance sign-off.

I’ve attached a short tax appendix template and our preferred PO acceptance language. Naomi/Ben — if Procurement is willing to do PO + VAT info, Legal can fast-track signatures.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
